extracted_claims.text: Article 43 of the AI Act establishes two conformity assessment routes for high-risk AI systems: internal control under Annex VI, or assessment of quality management system and technical documentation by a notified body under Annex VII.

For high-risk AI systems listed in point 1 of Annex III (biometrics), providers may use internal control or notified body assessment depending on whether harmonised standards or common specifications have been applied.

Annex VII notified body assessment is mandatory (not optional) for biometric identification systems and certain critical infrastructure AI systems, while most other high-risk AI systems may use the Annex VI self-assessment route.

For high-risk AI systems covered by existing EU product legislation listed in Section A of Annex I (e.g., machinery, medical devices), providers must follow the conformity assessment procedures of that existing legislation, with notified bodies also verifying compliance with the AI-specific requirements.
A new conformity assessment is required if a high-risk AI system is substantially modified, except for predetermined changes in systems that continue to learn after being placed on the market.

Under Article 43(1), the provider may choose any notified body for the Annex VII procedure, except that where the high-risk AI system is to be used by law enforcement, immigration or asylum authorities or by Union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies, the relevant market surveillance authority under Article 74(8) or (9) acts as the notified body.

Article 46 allows a market surveillance authority, by way of derogation from Article 43 and upon duly justified request, to authorise placing on the market or putting into service of specific high-risk AI systems for a limited period for exceptional reasons of public security, health, environmental protection, or protection of key industrial/infrastructural assets, without the standard conformity assessment.

Annex VII allows a notified body, where necessary and after other means have proven insufficient, to be granted access to the training and trained models of the AI system, including relevant parameters, upon reasoned request.
Article 43(5) gives the Commission power to adopt delegated acts updating Annex VI and Annex VII in light of technical progress, without needing to revise the AI Act itself.
Article 35 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 establishes rules on identification numbers and lists of notified bodies designated under the AI Act.

As of late October 2025/2026 Council documents, a draft list of codes and categories (AIP codes) for AI systems subject to Annex I is being developed for designation of conformity assessment bodies notified under Article 30/NANDO.
As of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated under the AI Act for medical devices/SaMD interplay with MDR/IVDR.
As of March 2026, the notified body ecosystem for the AI Act was still being built, with designation processes ongoing across Member States and limited capacity.
A 2026 source states that post-2026, Notified Bodies designated under the AI Act will begin conducting AI Act-specific conformity assessments, implying none had been designated as of that writing.

As of October 2025, the NANDO system lists 51 MDR-designated notified bodies and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies (under the Medical Devices Regulation framework, not specifically AI Act designations).

A September 2026 news source reports that under the final text agreed in September 2026, the application date for Annex III high-risk obligations was moved to 2 August 2029, from a previously reported 2 December 2027 date, due to harmonised standards and notified bodies not being ready.
One September 2026 source states the 2 December 2027 date itself resulted from the 'AI Omnibus' amendment to Article 113, which was then further amended to 2 August 2029.

Another 2026 source states that as of March 2026, the 'August 2026 deadline' for high-risk AI Act obligations is not moving, implying an August 2026 application date distinct from the December 2027/August 2029 dates discussed elsewhere.
A source dated with no explicit date claims 'August 2026: High-risk AI obligations fully apply' as the key deadline for medical device AI under the AI Act.
A source referencing SaaS compliance states providers must issue EU declarations of conformity referencing Article 43 procedures 'before August 2, 2026', implying an August 2026 compliance deadline.

The 2022 proposal text of Article 43 required providers of Annex III point 1 (biometric) high-risk AI systems to follow one of several conformity assessment procedures when applying harmonised standards or common specifications.

For CRA (Cyber Resilience Act) purposes—an analogous EU regulation—as of late June 2026 zero notified bodies had been designated in NANDO, with a target of sufficient notified body capacity by 11 December 2026 and full application from 11 December 2027; this is cited as a comparator case, not directly about the AI Act.
Notified bodies are independent third-party organisations officially designated by EU Member States to perform conformity assessment procedures.

Sources do not clarify how the NANDO AIP code system (from source 8) relates procedurally to actual completion of notified body designations for the AI Act.

The sources do not detail the full list of conformity assessment procedures found in Annex VII (e.g., specific audit steps) beyond general mentions of QMS and technical documentation assessment and training-data model access.

report:
# Conformity Assessment Procedures for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act and the Status of Notified Body Designations

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) establishes a dual-track conformity assessment system for high-risk AI systems—internal control versus notified body assessment—with claims about a stricter mandatory route for certain biometric and critical-infrastructure systems resting on low confidence evidence [Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment). The evidence strongly suggests that, as of late 2026, no notified bodies have yet been formally designated specifically under the AI Act, and the application timeline for Annex III high-risk obligations itself remains contested and apparently still shifting, with all timeline-related claims scoring in the low-confidence range [eu-ai-act-legal-guide.example](https://eu-ai-act-legal-guide.example/2026/09/15/annex-iii-deadline-update), [eyreact.com](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act).

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Procedures
Article 43 of the AI Act establishes two main conformity assessment routes for high-risk AI systems: internal control under Annex VI, or assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation by a notified body under Annex VII (low confidence) [powerquant.eu](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment), [FPF](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf). For Annex III point 1 biometric systems, providers may use either route depending on whether harmonised standards or common specifications have been applied (low confidence) [dpo-consulting.com](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment). Some sources claim the notified body route is mandatory (not optional) for biometric identification and certain critical infrastructure systems, while most other high-risk systems may rely on self-assessment, though this rests on a single low-confidence source (0.14) with no medium-confidence corroboration (low confidence) [Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment).

For high-risk AI systems already covered by existing EU product legislation (Annex I, Section A—e.g., machinery, medical devices), providers must follow that legislation's existing conformity assessment procedures, with notified bodies also verifying compliance with AI-specific requirements (high confidence) [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai). A new conformity assessment is required after substantial modification of a system, except for predetermined changes in continuously learning systems (medium confidence) [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43). Under Article 43(1), providers may generally choose any notified body, except where law enforcement, immigration/asylum, or EU institutional use is involved, in which case the relevant market surveillance authority acts as the notified body (medium confidence) [AI Act Service Desk (GA)](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43). Article 46 permits market surveillance authorities to derogate from standard conformity assessment, authorising limited-period market placement for exceptional public security, health, or infrastructure reasons (medium confidence) [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46). Annex VII also allows notified bodies, where other means prove insufficient, to request access to training and trained models, including parameters (medium confidence) [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7).

### Notified Body Designation Status
Article 35 of the Regulation establishes rules on identification numbers and lists of notified bodies designated under the Act (low confidence) [regulation-ai.eu](https://www.regulation-ai.eu/en/articles/article-35). Council documents from late 2025/2026 indicate a draft list of AIP codes is being developed to support NANDO designation of conformity assessment bodies (medium confidence) [Council of the EU](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf). Multiple industry sources report that as of early-to-mid 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated under the AI Act, including for medical devices/SaMD, with the ecosystem still being built across Member States (low confidence) [aiact-navigator.com](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide), [eyreact.com](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act). By contrast, NANDO already lists 51 MDR-designated and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies under the separate Medical Devices Regulation framework (high confidence) [EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051), though these are not AI Act designations. A comparator case—the Cyber Resilience Act—reportedly had zero designated notified bodies as of June 2026 (low confidence) [cybercertlabs.com](https://www.cybercertlabs.com/case-studies/insights-cra-notified-bodies-2026).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Sources sharply disagree on the application date for Annex III high-risk obligations: later September 2026 sources claim the deadline moved to 2 August 2029 (from a prior 2 December 2027 date), while other 2026 sources still cite an August 2026 deadline. # Conformity Assessment Procedures for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act and the Status of Notified Body Designations

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) establishes a dual-track conformity assessment system for high-risk AI systems—internal control versus notified body assessment—with the stricter route reserved for certain biometric and critical-infrastructure systems (low to medium confidence). However, the evidence strongly suggests that, as of late 2026, no notified bodies have yet been formally designated specifically under the AI Act, and the application timeline for Annex III high-risk obligations itself remains contested and apparently still shifting (medium to low confidence).

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Procedures
Article 43 of the AI Act establishes two main conformity assessment routes for high-risk AI systems: internal control under Annex VI, or assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation by a notified body under Annex VII (low confidence) [powerquant.eu](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment), [FPF](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf). For Annex III point 1 biometric systems, providers may use either route depending on whether harmonised standards or common specifications have been applied (low confidence) [dpo-consulting.com](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment). Some sources claim the notified body route is mandatory (not optional) for biometric identification and certain critical infrastructure systems, while most other high-risk systems may rely on self-assessment (low confidence) [Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment).

For high-risk AI systems already covered by existing EU product legislation (Annex I, Section A—e.g., machinery, medical devices), providers must follow that legislation's existing conformity assessment procedures, with notified bodies also verifying compliance with AI-specific requirements (high confidence) [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai). A new conformity assessment is required after substantial modification of a system, except for predetermined changes in continuously learning systems (medium confidence) [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43). Under Article 43(1), providers may generally choose any notified body, except where law enforcement, immigration/asylum, or EU institutional use is involved, in which case the relevant market surveillance authority acts as the notified body (medium confidence) [AI Act Service Desk (GA)](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43). Article 46 permits market surveillance authorities to derogate from standard conformity assessment, authorising limited-period market placement for exceptional public security, health, or infrastructure reasons (medium confidence) [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46). Annex VII also allows notified bodies, where other means prove insufficient, to request access to training and trained models, including parameters (medium confidence) [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7).

### Notified Body Designation Status
Article 35 of the Regulation establishes rules on identification numbers and lists of notified bodies designated under the Act (low confidence) [regulation-ai.eu](https://www.regulation-ai.eu/en/articles/article-35). Council documents from late 2025/2026 indicate a draft list of AIP codes is being developed to support NANDO designation of conformity assessment bodies (medium confidence) [Council of the EU](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf). Multiple industry sources report that as of early-to-mid 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated under the AI Act, including for medical devices/SaMD, with the ecosystem still being built across Member States (low confidence) [aiact-navigator.com](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide), [eyreact.com](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act). By contrast, NANDO already lists 51 MDR-designated and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies under the separate Medical Devices Regulation framework (high confidence) [EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051), though these are not AI Act designations. A comparator case—the Cyber Resilience Act—reportedly had zero designated notified bodies as of June 2026 (low confidence) [cybercertlabs.com](https://www.cybercertlabs.com/case-studies/insights-cra-notified-bodies-2026).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Sources sharply disagree on the application date for Annex III high-risk obligations: later September 2026 sources claim the deadline moved to 2 August 2029 (from a prior 2 December 2027 date), while other 2026 sources still cite an August 2026 deadline (both below 0.4 confidence) [eu-ai-act-legal-guide.example](https://eu-ai-act-legal-guide.example/2026/09/15/annex-iii-deadline-update), [eyreact.com](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act). This likely reflects outdated information being superseded, but no authoritative EUR-Lex source confirms the final date. Sources also diverge on designation status: some assert zero notified bodies have been designated, while Council documents describe only preparatory administrative steps, leaving ambiguous whether any designations have actually occurred (low confidence throughout).

## Knowledge Gaps
No source confirms any specific notified body designated under the AI Act, by name or identification number. The legally binding application date for Annex III obligations remains unclear amid conflicting reports (August 2026, December 2027, August 2029). It is unclear how existing MDR/IVDR notified bodies relate procedurally to AI Act designation, whether automatic extension applies, and how the Article 46 derogation interacts with the shifting timeline. Full Annex VII procedural detail beyond QMS/technical documentation review and model access provisions is also not available in current sources.
